I can honestly say that Bill Whittle changed who I am as a person.

I first discovered him in the immediate aftermath of 9/11, when I was looking for more information about what had happened and why. I think in a lot of ways he and I (and many others most probably) were going through the same philosophical transformation at the same time.

Why had it happened? Was it really all our fault as so many seemed to be saying at the time, and still do.

While never that naive, I still felt I needed to learn more. And Bill Whittle was a great person to learn from, and I will forever be indebted to him for having the courage to stand up and just speak truth.

He's only a few years older than I am, I believe. But I definitely look up to the man, and I like to think that's a rare thing.

Everything he says in this video is true. It just is. If you have a shred of sense in your head, you simply have to admit that, regardless of how you wish things could be...

If you really want to have your mind blown, try and find some of the essays a guy by the name of Steven Den Beste wrote around the same time Mr. Whittle was starting to speak.

There was a quote from a third party that Mr. Whittle had posted on his website back in the day, that more or less said, “If Steven Den Beste is Mr. Spock, then Bill Whittle is Captain Kirk.”

That’s pretty accurate. Mr. Whittle is no dummy by any stretch, but what he really excels at is inspiration. He’s a natural leader, albeit I think reluctantly, which I suppose is a characteristic all good leaders ironically share.

Mr. Den Beste was/is a very smart man, and a handful of the essays he produced back then are still some of the best words I’ve ever heard written on where we are and why.

I think he got sick, and semi-retired from serious writing, but if you like what Bill Whittle says here, then check out somebody who I think inspired him. (And me.)
